PullRequest.Title: Skip content exclusion checks for apply_patch Add File
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

`apply_patch` can reject `*** Add File` operations when a repository has Copilot exclusions configured because the target does not exist yet.

This change makes `apply_patch` Add File behavior consistent with `create_file`:

- Continue to enforce `allowedEditUris` for every target.
- Reject Add File when the target already exists.
- Skip content-exclusion checks only after confirming that the Add File target does not exist.
- Preserve existing exclusion checks for UPDATE, DELETE, and move operations.

## Testing

- `npm run typecheck`
- `npm run test:unit -- src/extension/tools/test/node/applyPatch/applyPatch.spec.tsx`

Added focused unit tests that verify:

- Add File succeeds without calling `IIgnoreService.isCopilotIgnored`.
- Add File outside `allowedEditUris` remains rejected before edits.
- Add File rejects an existing target without emitting edits.
- UPDATE operations continue to call the ignore service.
- Existing move tests continue to pass.

```text
Test Files  1 passed
Tests       13 passed
```

Fixes #337528

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed line, multi-operation grammar, serial loop, production service registration, and workspace.fs delegation are all directly traced. Exact provider latency and typical scaffold size vary, which affects severity but not the serial N-round-trip mechanism.
Findings.PerformanceResource: filesystem-provider/extension-host IPC calls issued by vscode.workspace.fs.stat
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The validation adds one awaited stat per distinct Add File section, and the nested for-loop serializes all N checks, so pre-edit latency grows as the sum of N filesystem-provider round trips.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: increased apply_patch latency and a longer blocked interval before any edits are emitted
Findings.PreviousBehavior: For Add File entries, this loop previously called only assertFileNotContentExcluded. When content exclusions are disabled, BaseIgnoreService returns false immediately; it did not issue a workspace.fs.stat for each destination.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Each Add File destination is now synchronously existence-checked with await this.fileSystemService.stat(uri) before the loop can inspect the next file or construct and emit edits.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added RIGHT line 291 introduces `await this.fileSystemService.stat(uri)` inside the loop over all commit file changes; the pre-diff code proceeded directly to the exclusion check and contained no existence-stat boundary on Add File destinations.
Findings.Title: Batch Add File existence checks instead of serializing filesystem round trips
Findings.Impact: A realistic agent scaffold that adds many files in a remote workspace or through a non-local filesystem provider waits for every destination stat in series before showing any edit. For N added files, users pay N provider/IPC latencies on the tool's critical path even though the checks are independent.
Findings.Evidence: The patch grammar explicitly permits one or more file operations and commit.changes retains one entry per distinct path. invoke builds fileChanges from all entries, then line 291 awaits stat inside the per-file loop. Production registers VSCodeFileSystemService, whose stat implementation directly returns vscode.workspace.fs.stat(uri), establishing the expensive provider boundary. No cache, grouping, or concurrency limiter coalesces these destination checks, and workspace edits are only constructed after this entire validation loop.
Findings.Recommendation: After preserving the current allowedEditUris checks, validate Add File destinations with bounded parallel workers (or a provider batch API if one exists), retain results in fileChanges order, and then throw for the first existing target before emitting edits. This preserves all-or-nothing validation while reducing critical-path latency from the sum of N round trips to bounded batches.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply a patch that scaffolds one or more new files at nonexistent destinations
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Patch parsing completes, allowedEditUris is checked, every Add File destination stat completes, and only then are workspace edits constructed and emitted. The new stats are directly on the user-visible apply critical path.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Check whether each Add File destination exists through vscode.workspace.fs.stat
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One call per distinct Add File destination, serialized; N calls for an N-file scaffold.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No destination stat was issued here; Add File proceeded through the exclusion check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: All N calls must settle before any workspace edit is built or emitted.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve content-exclusion policy through ignore service, potentially including Git repository lookup and batched CAPI rule fetch on a cold enabled cache
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Previously one exclusion decision per Add File target, with repository/rule/verdict caching; now zero for non-move Add File targets.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Add File awaited this exclusion decision; the PR skips it after the existence check.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: This previous boundary could block cold enabled-exclusion invocations, but is removed by the diff. With exclusions disabled the previous decision returned immediately.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Emit text edits through the chat response stream
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Existing edit emissions scale with changed files/edits.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Edits could be constructed immediately after exclusion validation, with no per-destination stat boundary when exclusions were disabled.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Pre-existing output work is now delayed until all newly added stats finish.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number N of distinct Add File sections in the patch after parser deduplication by path; cost is N provider stats.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The changed nested loops await each destination stat serially, so effective filesystem concurrency is 1. Edit emission also waits for all validations to finish.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The parsed commit may be reused from prepareInvocation, but destination existence results are not cached or coalesced. Each invocation performs fresh stats. The removed ignore path had cached repository/rule/verdict state when enabled and returned immediately when exclusions were disabled.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the added await is inside the per-file loop, multi-file patches are part of the documented grammar, production delegates stat to vscode.workspace.fs, and there is no batching or cache.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical Add File counts and filesystem-provider latency vary; local providers may make the delay small, while remote or extension-backed providers amplify each serialized round trip.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity boundary fan-out: independent provider stats are newly serialized on the pre-edit critical path.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply Add File when a destination already exists, or when allowedEditUris rejects a target
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Allowed URI validation runs first. A disallowed target returns before filesystem work. For an allowed Add File, stats run in file order and an existing target aborts before any edit emission.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Probe allowed Add File destinations for existence
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: Zero for an immediately disallowed URI; otherwise one per preceding Add File plus the existing target.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: No explicit existence probe occurred in this invoke validation loop.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: The probes determine rejection and occur before any edits are emitted.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Position of the rejected/existing target among N file changes; up to all preceding Add File targets are statted.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Serial validation with effective filesystem concurrency 1; processing stops at the first existing target.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: No existence cache is used. allowedEditUris is an in-memory ResourceSet and avoids the new boundary on rejection.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for boundary count and ordering; prevalence of late collisions is unknown.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Failure is usually found after few targets, but a late existing target can still incur most of the N serial probes.
Scenarios.Verdict: The same reported serial-fan-out mechanism covers late existing-target failures; the early allowedEditUris branch itself adds no regression.

Scenarios.Scenario: Apply update, delete, or move operations, including mixed patches
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Patch building opens source documents as before. Validation still checks allowedEditUris and content exclusions for update/delete and both move endpoints; only non-move Add File entries take the new stat branch.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Open source documents needed to parse updates/deletes
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One sequential open per distinct update/delete source, unchanged by the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same document opens occurred before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before commit validation and edits, unchanged.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Evaluate content exclusions for update/delete and move source/destination URIs
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One decision per affected URI, two for a move; cached/coalesced internally where applicable.
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Identical exclusion checks were performed before the PR.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Awaited before edits, unchanged for these operation types.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: Number of update/delete/move endpoints plus any Add File entries in a mixed patch.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: Validation remains serial across file changes and affected URIs. The diff changes boundary behavior only for Add File entries.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Ignore-service initialization is shared; repository/rule/verdict caches make warm exclusion checks cheaper. No new cache behavior applies to update/delete/move.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: the new condition excludes moves and non-ADD actions, leaving the prior call path intact.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Cold exclusion-policy costs depend on workspace and account configuration, but the PR neither adds nor increases them for these operations.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional performance finding for update/delete/move; their expensive boundaries and cardinality are unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Completed the performance pass over all changed files and diff pages. One introduced regression was submitted: multi-file Add File validation serializes newly added workspace filesystem stats before edit emission. Tests add no production cost, and update/delete/move paths retain their previous boundary behavior.
